approach.method_basis: The Parent is a task-local genetic search over molecular graphs with a Bayesian screening layer in front of the oracle. It keeps every molecule scored in the current task, breeds from the best of them by drawing parents from high-scoring score quantiles, and builds each candidate either by connected-fragment crossover between two scored molecules, optionally finished with one mutation, or by a short chain of random atom and bond edits; direct aromatic carbon-nitrogen exchange is switched off, a sulfur rule refuses any offspring that introduces an unusual sulfur environment its own scored parents did not already carry, candidates must survive a stable canonical identity check and both duplicate scopes, and the population greedily retains the best sixty-four molecules seen. For every announced batch of ten evaluations it first breeds a fresh field of 160 de novo offspring, fits a Gaussian process to the accepted scores of this task alone using a Tanimoto-style covariance over integer Morgan environment counts, then draws ten correlated samples of the fitted function over that whole field and emits the sampled maxima one at a time with the already chosen members masked out. Sixteen fresh candidates per evaluation has been the fixed ratio in every node of this lineage since the screening layer was introduced, and it is constant through the whole session: the two measured alternatives on this same Parent simply moved that constant up to sixty-four and down to four, and both lost score, the narrower one heavily.
approach.novelty: This Child makes the width of that candidate field depend on whether the search is still making progress. It keeps one plain counter of how many announced batches in a row have failed to raise the session's best score, counted against the best score that stood when each batch was announced and reset by any batch that beats it. While that counter stands at three or more, the next batch is screened over 640 fresh offspring instead of 160; on the first improving batch the inherited 160-member field returns. Nothing else moves: the same breeder, the same operators and probabilities, the same chemistry and identity filters, the same surrogate, kernel, noise, normalization and sampling law, and the counter itself consumes no randomness, so every decision a session makes before its first stall is identical to the Parent's, down to the random numbers drawn. The point is not that wider is better, which this Parent has already contradicted when applied to every batch: it is that extra candidate supply is only plausibly worth its cost in the roughly one fifth of batches where the inherited field has produced no new best molecule for three consecutive batches and delivers barely eight percent of the run's realized gain. This is the first node in the lineage whose behaviour varies with time inside a session; every earlier sibling, including the two width experiments, changed its parameter uniformly across all twenty-nine batches. The other three positions of this round use the same stall trigger but change how much the allocator trusts uncertainty, how far a local edit walks, and whether crossover is used at all; this one changes only how many fresh molecules compete, which is the one axis whose two endpoints are already measured on this exact Parent.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent is a complete matched panel: macro mean 0.596453 with population SD 0.033970, seed macros 0.643098, 0.563173 and 0.583088, and per-task means deco_hop 0.706940, drd2_docking 0.991017, median_2 0.222732, sitagliptin_mpo 0.604768 and zaleplon_mpo 0.456810 (n-1744a1494180). Reading its own fifteen published trajectories and stderr sessions, the limiting behaviour is that about a fifth of the oracle budget is spent inside episodes where the search has demonstrably stopped improving, and those batches are given exactly the same 160-member fresh candidate field as the batches that are already improving. Recomputed here from runs/SPIRAL2/nodes/n-1744a1494180/seed-0|1|2/trajectories/<task>.jsonl: a counter of consecutive announced batches that fail to raise the session best-so-far held when the batch was announced reaches 3 in 13 of 15 sessions (29 occurrences, 91 of 435 announced batches, never in deco_hop seeds 0 and 2), reaches 2 in 15 of 15 sessions (140 of 435 batches) and 4 in 12 of 15 sessions (62 of 435), while mean per-session best-so-far gain decays from +0.2402 over evaluations 11-100 to +0.1054 over 101-200 and +0.0424 over 201-300. Inside those 91 stalled batches, which carry 910 of the 4,350 oracle calls, the Anchor's own receipts give a strict generating-parent beating rate of 0.0857 against 0.1657 in unstalled batches and an incumbent-improvement rate of 0.0308 against 0.0660; only 25 of the 91 stalled batches raise the incumbent at all, their mean positive sequential increment is +0.0191 against +0.0312 elsewhere, and they hold 0.4766 of the Anchor's 5.819415 total sequential incumbent gain, that is 8.2 percent of realized gain for 20.9 percent of announced batches. Neither generation nor the selector is idle there: stalled batches average 175.03 breeding attempts (1.094 per admitted member) with no truncation, no exhaustion and no inherited escalation branch firing, and the ten choices are spread over the whole field (mean selected index 79.41 of 160, 85.8 percent of choices differing from the posterior-mean argmax, selected standardized posterior-mean enrichment +1.0731 against an available pool maximum of +1.7136). The consumer of that field is the Anchor's strongest measured component: removing the composite selector costs 0.128183 (n-605c7a785b51), removing its sampled residual costs 0.116317 (n-f04cec6ab705), removing cross-candidate correlation costs 0.050545 (n-8df0bb3bbcfe), and adding posterior selection originally gained 0.055880 (n-fc2c108a5253). So the component that pays for itself is handed no more material in the batches where it has stopped delivering than in the batches where it is already working, and the only two measured alternatives changed that width for the whole run: 640 everywhere lost 0.016060 (n-da0eeecfb462) and 40 everywhere lost 0.062417 (n-fe16bf000919).
hypothesis: While the session's own counter of consecutive non-improving announced batches stands at or above three, quadruple only the fresh offspring pool target per announced batch member, from sixteen to sixty-four (160 to 640 candidates at the announced batch of ten), so the unchanged accepted-only count-Tanimoto GP correlated Thompson allocator takes its ten sequentially masked joint-draw maxima over a four-times larger field of fresh de novo offspring produced by the unchanged breeder, operators, continuation, crossover and finishing, sulfur gate and identity admission; the inherited 160-member target is restored on the first announced batch whose accepted members raise the best-so-far that stood when it was announced. A batch is scored as improving or non-improving only from this session's accepted scores, the counter consumes no random numbers and changes no other law, so the mechanism can only alter values used while the trigger is active and every session reproduces the Parent exactly until its counter first reaches three.

finding_summary.headline: Widening the candidate field only during stalls ran exactly as designed, broke stalls sooner and cleared the +0.002 bar at +0.0047, on a thin margin
finding_summary.insights:
Candidate breadth is not wasted on this selector; its value depends on when it is spent. The earlier lesson that a fourfold field hurts needs restating. The always-640 variant's loss of 0.016 was almost entirely one lost rare breakthrough (deco_hop seed 0), and on the other 14 cells it was flat (+0.0004). On those same 14 cells, spending the extra breadth only during stalls averaged +0.005. So the right reading is "breadth is roughly neutral when spread across every batch and mildly helpful when concentrated where search has stopped improving", not a reversal from harmful to helpful. This node is also the lineage's first behaviour that changes with search state inside a session, and its clean implementation shows that such controls can be added without disturbing anything before they fire. That makes state-conditioned control a usable design axis.

How it helped matters for what to try next. The wider field did not produce better typical candidates or new chemistry: average offspring quality dipped, scaffold novelty was unchanged, and the molecular review found the same inherited halogenated fused-heteroaromatic families, with late budget spent on substituent variants. What improved was the tail. Among four times as many variants of the same families, the sampler found more that beat their parents, and by more, so short plateaus broke sooner. This lottery-like gain fits why it failed on the one long late plateau, and why spending breadth everywhere costs average quality without a matching payoff.

What remains open: the +0.0047 rests on two cells and one three-seed panel, so it clears the registered bar without yet being a robust effect. A repeat on independent seeds is the natural check before anything is built on it, not a threshold or width search, which the recipe rules out and nothing here justifies. This run tests trigger and width jointly, so it cannot say whether breadth helps whenever search stalls or whether this counter picked good moments. Because every K=3 stall-conditioned sibling this round leaves the same two deco_hop sessions untouched, all four share that protection, and sibling contrasts should be read on the 13 exposed cells. The width optimum and monotonicity remain unidentified.
finding_summary.results:
The trigger behaved exactly as registered. In all 435 announced batches the logged stall counter matched one recomputed from the scored molecules. The 86 batches that began after three or more non-improving batches each bred and ranked 640 fresh offspring, and the other 349 kept the usual 160. No pool was cut short, no numerical fallback occurred, every batch emitted ten molecules and every task used its 300 evaluations. Exposure landed close to the forecast from the Parent's runs: 86 widened batches in 32 stall episodes across 13 of 15 sessions, against 91 in 29. Before each session's first stall the run was the Parent's run, choice for choice. The two deco_hop sessions that never stalled reproduced all 300 Parent records, including the late seed-0 breakthrough to 0.856. Eight sessions first differed from the Parent exactly where predicted; five differed one evaluation later, because the first pick of the widened batch landed among the 160 candidates it shares with the Parent.

The extra candidates were used, not ignored. 73% of the picks in widened batches (627 of 860) came from beyond the first 160, spread almost evenly over all 640 positions, and those picks were as productive per pick as the rest. The wider field held better candidates: the model's top candidate stood further above the pool average (1.97 vs 1.71 standard deviations in the Parent's stalled batches). Unlike the earlier always-640 variant, the chosen molecules also moved up (1.17 vs 1.07), though they were somewhat more uncertain.

Stalled stretches became more productive on every registered measure. 31% of widened batches raised the session best, against 27% of the Parent's stalled batches. The average step when they did was +0.025 vs +0.019, and stalls broke after 2.4 batches instead of 3.2. Offspring beat their best parent 12.4% of the time vs 8.6%, by larger margins. Gains made inside stalls summed to 0.68 vs 0.48, which is 11.6% vs 8.2% of all improvement. The cleanest comparison is each session's first stall, which starts from an identical state in both runs. There the widened run broke out sooner in 5 sessions, later in 2 and at the same batch in 6, and its first widened batch produced twice as many parent-beating offspring (24 vs 12 of 130). The average offspring in widened batches was slightly worse (0.388 vs 0.405), and the rate of genuinely new scaffolds did not change, so the improvement came from the upper tail, not from a better typical candidate. Cost stayed small: 741 breeding attempts per widened batch instead of 175, mean non-oracle time 41 s per task instead of 26 s, and no node above 312 s against a 40,500 s limit. Peak memory was not recorded.

On the registered endpoint the matched mean rose from 0.5965 to 0.6011 (+0.0047, bar +0.002), positive on all three seeds (+0.003, +0.010, +0.001). Across the 15 task-seed cells there were 7 gains, 5 losses and 3 ties: the two never-stalled deco_hop sessions, and sitagliptin seed 2, where both runs independently found the same best molecule. Sitagliptin (+0.016) and median (+0.009) gained, deco_hop and zaleplon were flat, and drd2 slipped (-0.003). The margin is thin: without the best cell the rest average +0.0029, and without the best two they average +0.0015, below the bar. The worst cell is the most-widened session, zaleplon seed 0 (14 widened batches, -0.021). It found its best at evaluation 190 and then sat through eight widened batches to the end without improving, while the Parent found a better molecule at evaluation 281.

molecular.headline: Polyaromatic, halogen-decorated fused-ring molecules; leaders carry N-halogen, nitroso and transannular aromatic bonds
molecular.overall_character: Across all five objectives the node proposed 870 optimizer molecules per task (4,350 total, 3 seeds, 300 evaluations each) and every one parses as a valid neutral molecule. They are medium-sized and heavily cyclic: mean 23.7-32.1 heavy atoms, MW 357-475, 2.98-4.54 rings and 2.07-3.53 aromatic rings per molecule, consistent with the digest counters (ring_closure_rate 0.954-0.987, aromatic_atom_rate 0.945-0.976, branch_rate 0.955-0.984). Chemistry is elaborated almost entirely by decorating a fused heteroaromatic core with small substituents: methyl, ethyl, propyl, methoxy, hydroxymethyl, acetyl and above all halogen (digest halogen_rate 0.81-0.98 on four tasks, 0.10 on the fifth). The generator places halogen on heteroatoms as readily as on carbon: 951 of 4,350 proposals contain an N-halogen bond and 313 an O-halogen bond, while only 1 proposal in 4,350 contains a trifluoromethyl group and none an OCF3. No molecule carries a formal charge and none carries specified stereochemistry (digest charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0 on all five tasks), although RDKit finds unassigned stereocentres in 96.1 percent of the proposals on one task and in 100 percent of its top-scoring decile. Early exploration is broad (242-588 distinct Murcko scaffolds per 870 proposals) but the high-scoring decile collapses to 12-48 scaffolds, and on one task 43 of its 87 top molecules share a single scaffold. Two of the fifteen sessions, both on the same objective, are molecule-for-molecule identical to the Parent n-1744a1494180 for all 300 evaluations, so the Child's distinct chemistry comes from thirteen sessions.

per_task.generated_character: 870 proposals averaging 23.7 heavy atoms, MW 358, logP 3.85, TPSA 57, 2.98 rings and 2.40 aromatic rings. One family dominates: a methyl/ethyl/methoxy-substituted indole-2-carboxamide carrying an N-aryl amide, usually 3-pyridyl, elaborated from the initial molecule COc1cc2[nH]c(C(=O)Nc3ccc(F)cc3)cc2c(OC)c1OC. A second family replaces the indole with a benzimidazole and the amide with an aryl ketone (CCc1cc2c(nc(C(=O)c3cccc(Br)c3)n2Br)c(NC)c1OC) and a third with a propiolamide (COc1c(C)c2cc(c1C#CC(=O)N(Cl)c1cccc(F)c1)NCN2C). The top decile of 87 molecules spans only 12 Murcko scaffolds and 43 of them share O=C(Nc1cccnc1)c1cc2ccccc2[nH]1. Synthetic plausibility is low in the leaders because the amide and ring nitrogens are halogenated rather than N-H or N-alkyl.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds in 520 of 870 proposals and in 85 of the 87 highest-scoring molecules, including N-Br amides
Two-atom and one-atom species proposed as candidates, BrBr and C=NCl, both scoring 0.0
Propiolamide (ynone) Michael acceptors in 19 proposals, including a seed-2 leader
An N-chloro propiolamide on a non-aromatic cycloheptadiene ring, COc1c(C)c2cc(c1C#CC(=O)N(Cl)C1=CCCCC=C1)NCN2C, which stacks three liabilities on one molecule
missing_features: An unsubstituted N-H or N-alkyl amide in the leading family; the top decile has an N-halogen amide in 85 of 87 molecules
A free indole or azaindole N-H; the best molecules cap that nitrogen with F, Cl or Br instead
Solubilising polar groups: zero carboxylic acids and zero sulfonamides in 870 proposals, basic amines in only 30
Any trifluoromethyl or other polyhalogenated carbon substituent: zero in 870 proposals despite 266 N-F bonds
Ring-skeleton variation in the converged family; late evaluations change only terminal heteroatom substituents
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score climbs with size and aromatic ring count: the top decile averages 25.0 heavy atoms and 2.82 aromatic rings against 12.0 and 0.99 in the bottom decile, and with the presence of an aryl amide (72.4 percent of the top decile, 24.1 percent of the bottom). Within the leading family the score is flat to halogen identity: seven molecules tie at exactly 0.4828171386373609 and differ only in whether the ring and amide nitrogens carry F, Cl or Br and in OC versus CO on the benzo ring. The 0.0 floor is occupied by one- and two-atom fragments. The gradient rewards a lipophilic bicyclic heteroaromatic bearing one anilide-like amide, and it does not discriminate the halogen permutations the generator spends its late budget on.

per_task.generated_character: The largest and most polar molecules of the five tasks: 870 proposals averaging 32.1 heavy atoms, MW 475, logP 3.71, TPSA 127, 4.22 rings and 3.53 aromatic rings. Two families lead. The first is a fused triazolo-pyrimidinone bearing an N-linked quinazoline, decorated with hypofluorite, chloromethyl ether and thione: O=c1c2c3n(-c4ncnc5cc(OF)c(Cl)cc45)nc2n(c(=S)n1C(F)OCCl)C3. The second is an acetyl-substituted indolenine carrying two nitroso groups and a fused three-membered ring written as cc2-3, for example COCCc1c2c(c(C(N=O)Nc3cc4c(N=O)cc3-4)c(C)c1C(C)=O)N=C2. A seed-1 family is a benzoxazinone-linked biaryl with cyanate esters and an S-Br bond at MW 704. Seeds 0 and 2 reproduce the Parent trajectory exactly for all 300 evaluations, so only seed 1 contributes distinct chemistry. Essentially none of the leaders are makeable as written.
liabilities: A hypofluorite O-F bond in the highest-scoring molecule on this task, plus an alpha-chloro ether C(F)OCCl on the same molecule
Aryl and alkyl nitroso groups in 240 of 870 proposals and in over half the top decile
Cyanate esters OC#N and an S-Br bond in the seed-1 leader at MW 704, far outside drug-like space
Transannular bonds inside six-membered aromatic rings in 10.0 percent of all proposals and 25.3 percent of the top decile
One- and two-atom proposals Br, C=C and N=O consuming oracle calls at the 0.5 floor
missing_features: Amide or sulfonamide linkers between the ring systems: only 2.4 percent of proposals contain an amide and none a sulfonamide
Basic or ionisable centres for a molecule of MW 475 and TPSA 127: basic amines in only 3.8 percent of proposals
Conventional ortho-fused bicyclics in place of transannular aromatic bridges, which occur in a quarter of the top decile
Defined stereochemistry: 49.4 percent of proposals and 67.8 percent of the top decile have unassigned stereocentres
Carbon-bound polyhalogen substituents in place of the O-F and S-Br bonds the leaders use
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score rises with size and lipophilicity (top decile MW 517 and logP 5.12 against 275 and 1.84 in the bottom decile) and with three specific decorations: an aryl aldehyde or acetyl (51.7 percent of the top decile against 9.2 percent of the bottom), a nitroso group (55.2 against 5.7 percent) and an S-halogen bond (27.6 against 0.0 percent). The gradient also rewards topological complexity rather than clean fusion: 25.3 percent of the top decile contains a ring of four or fewer atoms whose atoms are all aromatic, that is a transannular bond drawn across a six-membered aromatic ring, and 11.5 percent contains a ring of eight or more atoms. The 0.5 floor is occupied by one- and two-atom species, so the objective gives no signal to shrink.

per_task.generated_character: 870 proposals averaging 30.4 heavy atoms, MW 452, logP 5.36, TPSA 46, 3.87 rings, 2.07 aromatic rings and fsp3 0.38, the most saturated and most lipophilic set of the five. One family dominates the leaders: a 2-arylhexahydro-pyrimidine or 1,4-diazepane aminal whose N1 carries an arylethyl chain and whose C2 carries a 3-chloro-4-fluorophenyl ring, as in CCCc1c(S)ccc(CCN2CCCCNC2c2ccc(F)c(Cl)c2)c1C and CC1Cc2ccc(CCN3CCCCNC3c3ccc(F)c(Cl)c3)cc21. A seed-2 family replaces it with an enamine-substituted dihydrobenzofuran. Scores are near-saturated: the best is 0.9999952 and the digest median is 0.7058. The basic amine and the dihalophenyl are recognisably drug-like; the aminal N-C-N centre and the benzocyclobutene fusion are not.
liabilities: Aminal N-C-N centres in 248 of 870 proposals and 72 of the 87 top molecules, labile to hydrolysis back to amine plus aldehyde
Free aryl thiol on a top-scoring molecule, CCCc1c(S)ccc(CCN2CCCCNC2c2ccc(F)c(Cl)c2)c1C
Primary and benzylic chloride alkylating groups in 153 of 870 proposals, including the final seed-2 molecule
An S-linked aminothiocarbamate, CCCCN(CCc1ccc2c(c1)CC2)C(N)Sc1ccc(F)c(Cl)c1, scored above 0.9999
Strained cyclobutane-fused benzene cores reached by ring contraction, as in CNC(CCOc1cc(F)cc2c1CC2)C1=CC(c2cc(O)cc(F)c2)C1
missing_features: A hydrolytically stable amine in place of the N-C-N aminal, which appears in 82.8 percent of the top decile
A single defined stereoisomer: 100 percent of the top decile has unassigned stereocentres at the C2 aminal carbon
Lipophilicity control: the top decile averages logP 5.36 and individual leaders reach 6.56
Ordinary five- and six-membered rings in place of the four-membered carbocycles fused to benzene that appear in 50 of the 87 top molecules
An explicitly protonated or salt form for a molecule whose activity depends on a basic centre; no proposal carries a formal charge
per_task.score_gradient_reading: This is the clearest gradient in the set and it is driven by one feature: a basic amine is present in all 87 molecules of the top decile and in only 14.9 percent of the bottom decile. Scores also rise as polarity falls (top decile TPSA 24.7 against 84.1) and as the sulfonamide and carboxylic-acid chemistry inherited from the initial molecules disappears: the bottom decile is 49.4 percent sulfonyl and 33.3 percent carboxylic acid, the top decile zero of each. Low-scoring proposals are the pyrrolidine sulfonamide fragments of the seed set, for example O=C(NCl)C1CCCN1S(=O)(=O)c1cc(Cl)cc(Cl)c1 at 0.000167. The objective rewards a lipophilic basic amine on a two-carbon linker between two aryl rings, and the generator found that pattern.

per_task.generated_character: 870 proposals averaging 30.8 heavy atoms, MW 422, logP 2.76, TPSA 77, 4.54 rings and 2.32 aromatic rings. This is the one task where the generator barely halogenates at all (digest halogen_rate 0.1011, 0.11 halogens per molecule) and instead builds large saturated nitrogen rings: 41 percent of proposals contain a ring of eight or more atoms and 33 percent contain a bridgehead atom. The leaders are a 2-propylquinoline or ethoxy-dibenzoxepine fused to an N,N-dimethylated bis-lactam, for example CCCc1c(OCC)ccc2c1NC(=C1CN(C)C(=O)CCN(C)CC1=O)c1ccccc1O2 and CCCc1cc(C2=C3C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)C4CNN(C)C(C(CC)C2)N34)c2ccccc2n1. Scores are compressed into a narrow band: best 0.2345 against a digest median of 0.1930, so the whole 300-evaluation budget moves the score by about 0.04.
liabilities: Eight-membered and larger rings with bridgeheads, conformationally undefined and hard to make, in 355 of 870 proposals
N-N single bonds, hydrazine-type, in 82 proposals including the seed-2 leader with its C4CNN(C) motif
Aminal N-C-N centres in 205 of 870 proposals, including the seed-2 leading family
An S-N bond in a final seed-2 molecule, CCCc1cc(C2=C3C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)C4CSNC(C(CC)C2)N34)c2ccccc2n1
Single-atom and two-atom proposals C and C#C scoring 0.0
missing_features: Any structure that reaches beyond 0.2345; the generator plateaus with three unrelated cores at 0.2298-0.2345
Halogen and aromatic substitution variety on this task: 0.11 halogens per molecule against 1.55-2.63 elsewhere
Medium-ring replacement by ordinary five- and six-membered fused rings; 79.3 percent of the top decile relies on an eight-plus ring
Acidic or sulfonamide polarity: 4 carboxylic acids and 1 sulfonyl group in 870 proposals
Defined configuration at the ring-fusion carbons; 62.9 percent of proposals carry unassigned stereocentres
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient is weak and almost entirely about the bis-amide ring: an amide is present in 97.7 percent of the top decile and 44.8 percent of the bottom, and a ring of eight or more atoms in 79.3 percent of the top decile against 3.4 percent of the bottom. Basic amines rise from 16.1 to 54.0 percent. Size and lipophilicity rise only slightly (32.4 heavy atoms and logP 3.43 against 26.2 and 1.98). No family reaches 0.25 and the three seeds converge on three different cores at nearly the same score, which reads as a plateau where the objective rewards a feature combination none of the generated families actually achieves.

per_task.generated_character: 870 proposals averaging 25.3 heavy atoms, MW 357, logP 2.00, TPSA 75, 3.57 rings, 2.47 aromatic rings and 2.01 halogens per molecule. The leading family is a polyfluorinated N-aryl pyrimidinone-triazinone bearing an exocyclic C=N imine and a quaternary fluorinated pyrrolinyl amine: COc1ccccc1-n1ccn(F)c(=N)n(F)c(=O)c(F)c1C1(F)C=CCN1 at 0.7124. A seed-2 family is a fused cyclopropa-pyrrolopyrimidinone with two fluoroethyl chains, Cc1c2c(=N)n(CCF)c(=O)n3c2c-3n1C1(F)C(O)=CC=C1CCF. The fluorine is almost all on nitrogen, oxygen or an isolated sp3 carbon: 344 proposals carry an N-F bond and 171 an O-F bond, while not one of the 870 carries a trifluoromethyl group or a trifluorinated arene. Nothing in the leading families would survive synthesis as drawn.
liabilities: N-F bonds on amidine and ring nitrogens in 344 proposals and 72 of the 87 top molecules, powerful oxidants rather than stable drug matter
O-F hypofluorite bonds in 171 proposals, including the seed-1 leader Cn1c(=NF)n(OF)c(=O)c2c(C3CC3(F)S)n(-c3ccccc3O)cc21
Allenes in 50 proposals, including the 0.6713 molecule COc1ccccc1-n1ccn(F)c(=N)n(F)c(=O)c(F)c1C1(F)C=C=CCN1
Transannular bonds in six-membered aromatic rings in 11.5 percent of the top decile, as in the seed-2 leading family
28 proposals of three or fewer heavy atoms, including F and FF, consuming oracle calls at the floor
missing_features: A trifluoromethyl group or a trifluorinated arene: zero of 870 proposals, against 344 with N-F and 171 with O-F
A beta-amino amide: only 2.2 percent of proposals contain any amide and none of the top decile does
Stereochemistry at the amine-bearing centre: 97.7 percent of the top decile has unassigned stereocentres
Saturated piperazine or triazolopiperazine rings in place of the C=N imine chains the gradient currently rewards
Carbon-framework fluorination that would survive aqueous conditions, in place of N-F and O-F bonds
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score tracks fluorine count almost monotonically: 3.79 halogens per molecule in the top decile against 0.86 in the bottom. It also tracks an exocyclic C=N imine (98.9 percent of the top decile against 11.5 percent of the bottom), an N-halogen bond (82.8 against 11.5 percent), a basic amine (64.4 against 13.8 percent) and size (27.7 heavy atoms against 13.9). The bottom decile is dominated by stripped fragments: 32.2 percent have three or fewer heavy atoms, with F and FF scoring about 1e-26. The objective rewards a heavily fluorinated nitrogen heterocycle with a primary or secondary amine, and the generator satisfies the fluorine count by fluorinating heteroatoms rather than by building a CF3 group.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Over the node's 4,350 optimizer proposals on five objectives (3 seeds, 300 evaluations each, read from the staging trajectories at /projects/standard/adeshwal/shared/zhou2577/SPIRAL/.worktrees/slot-3/runs/staging), 951 molecules contain an N-halogen bond and 313 an O-halogen bond, while exactly 1 contains a trifluoromethyl group and none an OCF3. On one objective 520 of 870 proposals and 85 of the 87 highest-scoring molecules carry an N-halogen bond; on another 344 carry N-F and 171 carry O-F, including a hypofluorite in that objective's highest-scoring molecule family and in the single highest-scoring molecule of a third objective (O=c1c2c3n(-c4ncnc5cc(OF)c(Cl)cc45)nc2n(c(=S)n1C(F)OCCl)C3). The same tendency is present in the Parent n-1744a1494180 trajectories (0 trifluoromethyl in 4,350 proposals), so this is inherited, not introduced.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator forms halogen bonds to nitrogen and oxygen as freely as to carbon, and cannot build a polyhalogenated carbon substituent.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Halogen substitution is the operator set's cheapest edit and it is applied without regard to the element it attaches to. A task-agnostic generator would treat heteroatom-halogen bond formation as a distinct rarely valid class rather than one more substitution, and would offer the ordinary alternatives in its place: halogen on carbon, geminal polyhalogenation to give a stable CF3 or OCF3, or leaving the heteroatom as N-H or N-alkyl. Both directions matter, because objectives that reward halogen content currently get satisfied by the unstable placement and objectives that reward a stable lipophilic carbon substituent cannot be reached at all.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On one objective 10.0 percent of 870 proposals and 25.3 percent of the top-scoring decile contain a ring of four or fewer atoms every atom of which is aromatic, that is a bond drawn across the interior of a benzene ring (COCCc1c2c(c(C(N=O)Nc3cc4c(N=O)cc3-4)c(C)c1C(C)=O)N=C2, CC(=O)c1c(C)c(C(N=O)Nc2cc3c(N=O)cc2-3)c2c(c1CCOC=S)C=N2). On a second objective the figure is 11.5 percent of the top decile, and on a third 41 percent of all proposals and 79.3 percent of the top decile contain a ring of eight or more atoms, with 33 percent carrying bridgeheads (CCCc1c(OCC)ccc2c1NC(=C1CN(C)C(=O)CCN(C)CC1=O)c1ccccc1O2 fuses a 7- and a 9-membered ring). Every proposal is valence-valid and parses, so the failure is geometric, not syntactic.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-editing operators create transannular bonds inside six-membered aromatic rings and eight- to ten-membered rings without any geometric feasibility check.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring formation, ring bridging and ring contraction are currently validated by valence and canonical identity only. A task-agnostic generator would need ring-size and planarity awareness in those operators: refuse a new bond between two atoms of the same aromatic ring, bound medium-ring formation unless the closure is conformationally reachable, and supply an ordinary ortho-fused bicyclic as the alternative edit so that the topological complexity the objectives reward can be reached through feasible scaffolds.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest counters give charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0 on all five objectives over 870 proposals each. Structural perception of the same molecules finds unassigned stereocentres in 96.1 percent of the proposals on one objective and in 100 percent of its top decile (CC1Cc2ccc(CCN3CCCCNC3c3ccc(F)c(Cl)c3)cc21 has two), 97.7 percent of the top decile on a second (COc1ccccc1-n1ccn(F)c(=N)n(F)c(=O)c(F)c1C1(F)C=CCN1) and 67.8 percent on a third. On the objective where a basic amine appears in all 87 top-scoring molecules, not one is written in a protonated or salt form.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits no charged species and no specified stereochemistry, yet most of its best molecules have stereogenic centres and basic centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The representation cannot express configuration or protonation state, so every sp3 centre the operators build is an undefined mixture and any objective that distinguishes enantiomers, diastereomers or ionisation state is being scored on an ambiguous structure. A task-agnostic generator would either assign configuration when it creates a stereogenic centre and carry it through crossover and mutation, or explicitly mark the centre as racemic, and would be able to propose a charged or zwitterionic form where the neutral notation is not the physiological one.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across the five objectives the proposals include nitroso groups in 240 of 870 molecules on one objective, with over half its top decile nitroso-bearing; allenes in 50 of 870 on another, one of them scoring 0.6713 (COc1ccccc1-n1ccn(F)c(=N)n(F)c(=O)c(F)c1C1(F)C=C=CCN1); alpha-halo ethers and thiones in the single highest-scoring molecule of a third; aminal N-C-N centres in 248 of 870 on a fourth, including 72 of its 87 top molecules; primary and benzylic chlorides in 153 of that same set; and cyanate esters with an S-Br bond in a 0.6240 molecule (Cc1c(Oc2cccc(-c3cc(CBr)cc(SBr)nc(=S)ocn3)c2)nc2oc(=O)nc(OC#N)c2c1OC#N). An aryl thiol sits on a molecule scoring 0.9999952 (CCCc1c(S)ccc(CCN2CCCCNC2c2ccc(F)c(Cl)c2)c1C).
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has no notion of functional-group stability and routinely attaches reactive or short-lived groups to otherwise reasonable scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Admission currently tests valence, canonical novelty and one narrow inherited sulfur rule, and nothing else about chemical stability. A task-agnostic generator would classify the local environment it is creating against a general reactivity and stability vocabulary covering N-O, O-halogen, N-halogen, cumulated double bonds, aminals, alkylating benzylic halides and pseudohalide esters, and would propose a conventional isostere that preserves the size, polarity and substitution pattern the objective is rewarding instead of simply rejecting the edit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: 104 of the node's 4,350 proposals have three or fewer heavy atoms and 142 have six or fewer. They include C, C#C, F, FF, BrBr, Br, C=C, N=O and C=NCl, and they are proposed as late as evaluation 298 of 300. On one objective 32.2 percent of the bottom-scoring decile is three heavy atoms or fewer. Each sits at the objective's floor: C and C#C at 0.0, F at about 1.1e-26, Br and C=C at the 0.5 constant floor of another objective. The Parent n-1744a1494180 shows the same behaviour, so the capability gap is inherited.
transferable_gaps.gap: Deletion operators can strip a candidate to one or two atoms, and such fragments are proposed to the oracle rather than repaired.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Atom and ring deletion is unbounded below, so a fraction of every objective's fixed evaluation budget is spent on molecules too small to carry any pharmacophore. A task-agnostic generator would bound deletion by a minimum heavy-atom count or by retention of at least one ring system, and would re-attempt the edit instead of emitting the fragment, which costs nothing in representation and returns those calls to candidates that can carry signal.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On one objective seven molecules tie at exactly 0.4828171386373609 and differ only in whether two nitrogens carry F, Cl or Br and in OC versus CO on the benzo ring (CCc1c(OC)cc2c(cc(C(=O)N(F)c3cccnc3)n2F)c1C and COCc1c(C)cc2c(cc(C(=O)N(Br)c3cccnc3)n2F)c1C are two of them); a second session on the same objective has nine molecules tied at its best. Its top-scoring decile of 87 molecules spans 12 Murcko scaffolds with 43 sharing one, and on another objective the top decile spans 25 scaffolds with 19 sharing one, against 242-588 distinct scaffolds in the full proposal set. Nine of the fifteen top-29 windows contain fewer than 25 distinct scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: Once a family is found the generator varies only terminal heteroatom substituents, producing analogues the objective scores identically.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The edit distribution concentrates on substituent identity at a few peripheral heteroatoms, which is the cheapest edit and the one least likely to move any objective. A task-agnostic generator would need edits that change the ring skeleton, the linker length and the fusion pattern at comparable frequency, and a way to recognise that a proposed analogue differs from an already-evaluated molecule only by a substitution class that has repeatedly returned an identical score, so that late budget buys new chemistry rather than permutations of the incumbent.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All five objectives start from the same ten initial molecules, yet basic amine content in the 870 proposals ranges from 502 of 870 on one objective, where all 87 top-scoring molecules carry one (CCCc1c(S)ccc(CCN2CCCCNC2c2ccc(F)c(Cl)c2)c1C), down to 30 of 870 on another and 33 on a third. Amide content ranges from 716 of 870 on one objective to 19 on another, where none of the top decile contains an amide at all. Carboxylic acids and sulfonamides are present essentially only in the early descendants of the one seed molecule that carried them, and vanish from every top decile.
transferable_gaps.gap: Basic amine and amide chemistry appears only where the early accepted molecules already carried it, and is not introduced de novo elsewhere.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Whole functional-group classes are reachable only by inheritance from the initial molecules, not by construction, so a session that drifts away from a group early can never recover it even when it is the feature the objective rewards. A task-agnostic generator would need operators that install common polar and ionisable motifs as a unit, amine, amide, sulfonamide and acid, onto whatever scaffold is current, rather than relying on single-atom edits to rediscover them.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Accepted-only chronological archive, greedy 64-member survivor population and score-quantile parent sampling (edges 0.10/0.25/0.50, weights 0.60/0.30/0.10).

Connected-fragment crossover (p 0.45, halved after 40 member attempts) with optional finishing mutation (p 0.35), ordinary mutation continuation [1, 2, 3] with weights [0.82, 0.15, 0.03] and the member_attempts // 80 escalation, seven atom/bond/ring operator families with unchanged probabilities and twelve internal retries; the halving and escalation branches never fired here.
Disabled direct aromatic C/N exchange, stable canonical/isomeric identity admission, emitted/initial and temporary-pool duplicate rejection, max 120 atoms.
Sulfur valence-environment introduction gate using the per-signature maximum over the original scored generating parents.

Radius-2 chirality-aware 2048-bin integer Morgan-count features, generalized dot-product Tanimoto GP fitted only to accepted labels, adaptive mean and population-SD normalization with 0.001 floor, noise SD 0.05, float64 covariance with the Cholesky jitter ladder, correlated Thompson allocation with sequential availability masks and first-index ties.
Identity-bound predictions, pending accepted-feedback joins, next-fit probes, fixed batch/budget/profile and the generation-order numerical fallback (never triggered).

New: stall-conditioned fresh-pool breadth. A counter of consecutive announced batches that fail to raise the session best-so-far held at announcement, read from this session's accepted scores and consuming no randomness, sets the pool target to 640 while it stands at three or more and 160 otherwise; the first improving batch restores 160.
